result.topic_en: Calculations on the theta function: its definition as an exponential series, its behaviour under shifts of the arguments by periods and half-periods (theta characteristics with 0/1 tables), and expressions of the roots of products of linear forms, such as $\sqrt{xyz}$-type quotients, as constants times theta quotients.

methods.what: Definition of the p-variable theta function as an exponential series over integer vectors
methods.quote: $\vartheta(v_1,v_2,\dots v_p) = \Sigma e^{\Sigma a_{\mu\mu'} m_\mu m_{\mu'} + 2\Sigma m_\mu v_\mu}$

methods.what: Series for theta with arguments shifted by half-periods (theta with characteristic g, h)
methods.quote: $\Sigma e^{\Sigma a_{\mu\mu'}(m_\mu + h_\mu)(m_{\mu'} + h_{\mu'}) + 2\Sigma(m_\mu + h_\mu)(v_\mu + g_\mu \pi i)}$

methods.what: Quasi-periodicity of theta under shifts by periods
methods.quote: $\vartheta(v_\mu + \pi i) = \vartheta \quad \vartheta(v_1 + a_{1,\mu}, v_2 + a_{2,\mu}, \dots) = \vartheta . e^{-2v_\mu - a_{\mu\mu}}$

methods.what: Transformation factor of a quotient of theta functions with characteristics under a period shift
methods.quote: $\frac{\vartheta'}{\vartheta}(v_1 + a_{1,\mu}, v_2 + a_{2,\mu}) = \frac{\vartheta'}{\vartheta} . e^{-2g_\mu \pi i - 2\Sigma h_{\mu'} a_{\mu\mu'}}$

methods.what: Expression of the square root of a quotient of linear forms as a constant times a theta quotient, with the constant given as a fourth root
Determination of the constant A by evaluating at x=0 and t=0
Relation among linear forms satisfying linear relations, giving the root of a product of forms
Linear relations among six linear forms with parameters
Quotient formula involving the quartic $f^2=xyzt$ expressed through square roots of the forms
methods.quote: $\frac{x_1 y_1 f - f_1 x y}{x_1 z_1 f - f_1 x z} \sqrt{\frac{z z_1}{y y_1}} = \frac{\sqrt{z t x y_1} - \sqrt{z_1 t_1 x y}}{\sqrt{y t x_1 z_1} - \sqrt{y_1 t_1 x z}}$

methods.what: Theta quotient representation of a root of products of forms evaluated at four points
methods.quote: $\frac{f + y(x, y, z)}{f + z(x, y, z)} \sqrt{\frac{z z_1 z_2 z_3}{y y_1 y_2 y_3}} = A \frac{\vartheta}{\vartheta}$
